title: Ferrous sulfate reduces thyroxine efficacy in patients with hypothyroidism
authors: Campbell NR, Hasinoff BB, Stalts H, Rao B, Wong NC
population: Patients with established primary hypothyroidism on stable thyroxine at a tertiary outpatient research clinic in Calgary; uncontrolled clinical trial
funder: Funding statement not read: the publisher's full text returned HTTP 403 to automated access.
result: After 12 weeks of a 300-mg ferrous sulfate tablet taken together with thyroxine, mean TSH rose from 1.6 to 5.4 mU/l (P < 0.01) while the free thyroxine index did not change significantly; 9 of 14 patients had more symptoms and signs of hypothyroidism. Mixed in vitro, iron and thyroxine formed a poorly soluble complex. Results read from the PubMed abstract.
